title: Install/uninstall card move lags seconds behind the toast - it waits on a disk-stat round trip
description: Reported by the user 2026-07-29 on a remote Pod: pressing Uninstall fires the toast and drops the sidebar card immediately, but the model stays under Installed for several seconds before the grid catches up. CONFIRMED BIDIRECTIONAL 2026-07-30 - an INSTALL behaves the same way: the completion toast landed at about 7 seconds and the card took about 10 to move sections. Same root, so fix both directions or neither; the card title said uninstall only and understated it. It reads as buggy. This is NOT a rendering bug and must not be fixed as one. Install-state is DERIVED by statting disk, never stored (docs/model-library.md line 53: install-state IS files-on-disk, there is no persisted install record), so model.installed stays true until syncModelInstalled completes a /comfy/models/check - which on a remote engine is a round trip to the Pod wrapper over the internet. That round trip IS the lag. Confirming the shape: MpiModelManager's download:uninstalled handler is the only terminal download handler with no _patchTile / awaitReSync (download:cancelled, download:complete and download:failed all have one), but adding one would change nothing, because at that instant model.installed is still true and _patchTile re-renders from the same stale flag. Making this feel instant requires an OPTIMISTIC local install-state flip on download:uninstalled (the route already returns a truthful removed[] / kept* to drive it), reconciled by the re-sync that follows. That deliberately relaxes the disk-truth invariant the earlier download refactors were built around, so it is a product decision, not a bug fix - hence idea, not planned. Related but separately rooted: MPI-396.
acceptance: Decide first: is an optimistic install-state flip acceptable against the install-state-IS-files-on-disk invariant
If yes - uninstall moves the model to Available within one frame, driven by the route's truthful removed[] response
The following re-sync reconciles, and a partially-failed or remote-unsupported uninstall snaps the model back rather than leaving the UI lying
Local and remote engines behave the same
